uncited: *   **Input:** A set of 3D Gaussians (means, covariances, opacities, spherical harmonic coefficients) initialized from a standard 3DGS or 3DGS-MCMC training run; input images for complexity estimation.
*   **Output:** A sorted list of primitives based on a computed "complexity" metric, allowing any prefix of the list to be rendered to achieve a specific budget (primitive count).
*   **Complexity Map:** A precomputed field associated with each Gaussian.
*   **Primitive Ordering:** A static array of indices sorted by descending complexity.
Compute complexity maps once per scene before training.
This is implemented in PyTorch on the GPU.
*   Use a fixed receptive field of 32 pixels.
*   Use a stride of 4 to 8 pixels depending on image resolution.
Initialize Gaussians from a standard 3DGS or 3DGS-MCMC checkpoint.
*   If $t < 500$: Render the training view at full capacity (all primitives).
*   Compute the loss $L$ using the formula below.
*   Apply complexity dropout during relocation selection with rate $\delta=0.2$.
*   $L_{rec}$ is the L1+D-SSIM loss of 3DGS.
*   $\hat{I}_i^{full}$ is the rendered image at full capacity.
*   $\hat{I}_i^{\tau}$ is the rendered image at budget $\tau$.
*   $\bar{\alpha}$ is the mean opacity of the primitives.
*   $\bar{\sigma}$ is the mean scale of the primitives.
*   $\lambda_{var}, \lambda_{\alpha}, \lambda_{\sigma}$ are weighting hyperparameters.
*   **New/Relocated Gaussians:** A newly added or relocated Gaussian has no complexity estimate until a training view observes it.
*   **Complexity Dropout:** The dropout rate $\delta$ interpolates between applying complexity always ($\delta=0$) and dropping it always ($\delta=1$, reducing to original opacity sampling).
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the complexity map for each Gaussian.
No additional hierarchical data structures are needed compared to standard 3DGS.
*   **Strengths:** Continuous LoD allows any budget within the range; progressive streaming is enabled by the fixed ordering; view-independent selection simplifies deployment.
*   **Limitations:** Requires a one-time pre-processing step; the ordering is fixed, so it may not adapt to specific camera viewpoints as well as camera-dependent methods.
